facts.text: After slavery, about **2 million** Indians went abroad as **indentured labour** (1838-1917). **Shashi Tharoor** called the omission of colonialism 'inexcusable' (he once proposed a symbolic **£1 a year for 200 years**). Barbados (PM **Mia Amor Mottley**) became a republic in **2021**.

facts.text: UK PM **Andy Burnham** said he is open to a **formal apology for the slave trade** but ruled out reparations; ex-PM **Gordon Brown** will lead a debt initiative for poor Commonwealth nations. Britain abolished the slave trade in **1807** and slavery in **1833** (freedom by 1838), paying slave owners **£20 million**.

facts.text: **Serbia**: the student movement born of the **1 Nov 2024 Novi Sad** railway canopy collapse (16 dead; a Belgrade-Budapest rail project backed by China's **BRI**) won the **25 Oct** snap election — the **'Student List'** took **141 of 250** seats against **103** for **Aleksandar Vucic's SNS**, ending 14 years of SNS rule. Lead candidate: cardiologist **Ilija Srdanovic**.

facts.text: Thousands of students and workers protested across **Italy** over school funding and cost of living, with a general strike by the **USB** union, following similar movements in France and Spain.

facts.text: Russian newspaper **Novaya Gazeta** shut down, citing Kremlin pressure; its founder **Dmitry Muratov** shared the **2021 Nobel Peace Prize** with Maria Ressa.

facts.text: Youth-led protests are spreading in Europe: France (since mid-Sept, over schools and cost of living; youth unemployment above 20%), Spain (housing), Serbia (two years of leaderless student protests that toppled the government) and Albania.
